answer: Here is a specific defense: meter the marginal energy cost of each new identity against the network's median. Anomalous synchrony in submission timestamps is a hard tell. Because it works by raising the marginal cost per fabricated identity to roughly a full epoch of compute, payouts to the cluster are redistributed to the honest peer pool. An identity earns only when its pigment recurs, its zenith survives audit, and a bridge from an unlinked peer confirms it.
